reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction from Hassabis in 2015 that meets all four tests. The closest material is one interview transcript dated 21 October 2015. In it he gives one AGI timing remark ("many decades away"), which I've listed under undated. He also gives two "in a few months" remarks about Go and DeepMind announcements.

**What the 2015 transcript holds.** The source is a PDF transcript of a call between Hassabis and Dario De Toffoli, a games friend. It is hosted on studiogiochi.com, De Toffoli's own company's site, so it is not an official DeepMind record. In it:
- **Go:** De Toffoli says "maybe we will have a surprise about go...", and Hassabis answers: "yes, we will. I think in a few months there will be quite a big surprise." He also says DeepMind would make "other big announcements" "in a few months time". "A few months" is as vague as "soon", and these lines are not about AGI, so I left them out of every list. In hindsight the Go line points to AlphaGo, which was published in January 2016. You may decide otherwise.
- **AGI:** About "solving intelligence" he says "it's many decades away, the full thing...". I treated "many decades" as undated, like "a few years", and put it under undated. If you count it as a length of time, it would move to candidates.

**What didn't open or wasn't checked:**
- Steven Levy's January 2015 interview "The Deep Mind of Demis Hassabis" (Backchannel on Medium) is the most likely place for more 2015 timing claims. I found its address only inside a search result. The tool refused to open it because that address wasn't the result's own link, and the Hacker News page linking to it also wouldn't open. I have not quoted it.
- The NBC News article on the 2015 Atari work would not open. The Christian Science Monitor article opened, but none of its Hassabis quotes were predictions; the one forward-looking line ("a few tweaks") was the researchers', not his.
- I didn't watch his IET public lecture video (published 19 November 2015).
- All 12 searches were used. Most returned 2023–2026 news.

The quotes come from text pulled out of the PDF, so check them against the page itself.
